claim_text: Pi configures from JSON settings files in which project settings override global ones.
evidence_span: Pi uses JSON settings files with project settings overriding global settings.

claim_text: Relative resource paths in a Pi settings file resolve against that file's own directory — ~/.pi/agent for global settings and .pi for project settings — with absolute paths and ~ also accepted.
evidence_span: Paths in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` resolve relative to `~/.pi/agent`. Paths in `.pi/settings.json` resolve relative to `.pi`. Absolute paths and `~` are supported.

claim_text: Pi's resource arrays in settings take glob patterns plus explicit overrides: !pattern excludes, +path force-includes an exact path, and -path force-excludes one.
evidence_span: Arrays support glob patterns and exclusions. Use `!pattern` to exclude. Use `+path` to force-include an exact path and `-path` to force-exclude an exact path.

claim_text: Pi advises leaving retry.provider.maxRetries at 0, because provider-level retries can swallow out-of-usage-limit errors before Pi sees them and block the agent until the provider quota resets.
evidence_span: Keep `retry.provider.maxRetries` at `0` unless provider-level retries are explicitly needed. Setting it above `0` can make SDK/provider retries handle out-of-usage-limit errors before Pi sees them, which may block the agent until the provider quota resets in some circumstances.

claim_text: Pi's enableInstallTelemetry governs the anonymous install/update ping and provider attribution headers only; opting out leaves version-check requests running, which PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK or offline mode disables separately.
evidence_span: `enableInstallTelemetry` controls the anonymous install/update ping to `https://pi.dev/api/report-install` and Pi attribution headers for OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, and Cloudflare provider requests. Opting out disables both. It does not disable update checks
